s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of shortness of breath and palpitations in a patient with a history of cardiovascular disease
salient_findings: Supraventricular tachycardia with a rate of 120 beats per minute
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
History of hypertension
History of hyperlipidemia
History of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
History of moderate pulmonary hypertension
Patient takes aspirin, atorvastatin, amlodipine, tiotropium, and a budesonide-formoterol inhaler
Left ventricular ejection fraction of 40% compared with 60% 2 months prior
25% narrowing of the left anterior descending artery
Distally occluded right coronary artery
Supraventricular tachycardia with subtle retrograde P waves
RR interval of 800ms in sinus rhythm
PR interval of 200ms in sinus rhythm

shortlist.label: Supraventricular Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has supraventricular tachycardia with subtle retrograde P waves and a rate of 120 beats per minute

shortlist.label: Atrioventricular Nodal Reentrant Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's ECG shows initiation and termination patterns of tachyarrhythmia consistent with AVNRT

shortlist.label: Ischemic Cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and coronary artery disease, with a decreased left ventricular ejection fraction

shortlist.label: Dilated Cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a decreased left ventricular ejection fraction and a history of cardiovascular disease

shortlist.label: Atrioventricular Reentrant Tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's ECG shows subtle retrograde P waves during tachyarrhythmia, consistent with AVRT

raw.rationale: The patient's ECG shows a regular narrow complex supraventricular tachycardia with subtle retrograde P waves, and the initiation and termination patterns of the tachyarrhythmia are consistent with AVNRT, particularly the change in PR interval preceding the onset of tachycardia.

rejected.label: Supraventricular Tachycardia
rejected.why: Too broad, as the ECG findings suggest a more specific diagnosis

rejected.label: Ischemic Cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: While the patient has coronary artery disease, the primary issue presented is the tachyarrhythmia, not the cardiomyopathy

rejected.label: Dilated Cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The left ventricular ejection fraction is decreased, but the primary clinical issue is the tachyarrhythmia, and dilated cardiomyopathy is not directly implicated in the ECG findings

rejected.label: Atrioventricular Reentrant Tachycardia
rejected.why: The ECG findings, particularly the subtle retrograde P waves during tachycardia, are more suggestive of AVNRT than AVRT, which typically involves an accessory pathway
